title: Executive Override with Missing Post-Authorization Review
scenario_text:
During year-end SOX testing, you're evaluating management override controls at Ironforge. Your analytics flagged a transaction where the normal three-way match was bypassed. The evidence trail spans six weeks and multiple systems:

**SAP S/4HANA — Transaction FB03 (Document Display), Doc 1900045521**
Posting date: 2025-12-18 | Type: KR (Vendor invoice) | Amount: $347,200
Vendor: Precision Alloys International (VM-00298) | Text: 'Emergency titanium bar stock — Lot TI-6AL4V-2025-889'
Posted by: R.VASQUEZ (VP Operations) | Override reason code: 'OP-NECS' (Operational Necessity)
Three-way match status: Bypassed | GR reference: None | PO reference: None
[SAP override log — SM21: Override authorization used; control bypass recorded per SoD exception SA-2025-041]

**MasterControl — SoD Exception Register**
SA-2025-041: R.VASQUEZ granted temporary override for AP posting (conflict: requisitioner + approver + poster)
Effective: 2025-12-15 | Expiry: 2025-12-31 | Condition: 'All overrides require documented post-review by Controller within 5 business days per POL-FIN-008 Section 4.6'
Approved by: CFO (C.Morrison) on 2025-12-14

**SharePoint — /finance/policies/POL-FIN-008-Management-Override-Controls-Rev4.docx**
Section 4.6: 'When management override is exercised under operational necessity, the following compensating controls apply: (a) Controller must perform independent review within 5 business days; (b) Review must be documented in the override log with sign-off; (c) Failure to complete review within 5 business days escalates to Audit Committee.'
[Document version history: Rev 4 published 2025-09-01. Rev 3 stated '10 business days' — changed to 5 per audit committee direction after prior year finding.]

**SAP — Override Review Log (Custom Z-table ZOVERIDE_REV)**
Doc 1900045521 | Override date: 2025-12-18 | Review due: 2025-12-26 (5 business days, excluding Dec 24-25 holidays)
Reviewer assigned: K.WRIGHT (Controller) | Review status: OPEN | Review date: [blank]

**Microsoft Teams — DM between K.Wright and F.Owens (2026-01-08)**
@K.Wright: Hey Franklin — just flagging, I'm working through the Dec override reviews now. Got backed up with year-end close. The Vasquez one from 12/18 — I talked to him about it before the break and it's legit, but I haven't put the formal sign-off in the system yet. Will do it this week.
@F.Owens: 👀
[No further messages]

**Outlook — R.Vasquez to Procurement (2025-12-17, 6:44 PM)**
Subject: URGENT — titanium shortage for Aerojet lot
'Team — our TI-6AL4V supplier shorted us on the last delivery and we're 3 days from halting the Aerojet line. I found bar stock at Precision Alloys but they won't hold it past tomorrow. I'm going to push this through directly. Will sort the paperwork after. Raj — can you backfill the PO?'
[Reply from Raj (2025-12-18, 8:01 AM): 'PO created — 4500091002. You'll need to link it to the invoice.']
[No evidence the invoice was ever linked to PO 4500091002 in SAP.]
question: As of the audit fieldwork date (January 10, 2026), what is the status of this override finding?

contributor.name: Franklin Owens
contributor.title: Internal Audit Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: SOX compliance, management override testing, compensating control evaluation, segregation of duties

choices: Significant deficiency — the compensating control required by the SoD exception failed (no documented review within 5 business days), the review was not escalated to Audit Committee as required by POL-FIN-008 Section 4.6, and the invoice remains unmatched to the PO; the verbal Teams message cannot substitute for the required documented sign-off

Control deficiency — the compensating control (5-day review) was not completed timely, but the verbal confirmation in Teams and the retroactive PO creation demonstrate the underlying transaction is legitimate
No finding — the override was properly authorized via SoD exception SA-2025-041, the operational necessity is well-documented in email, and the Controller verbally confirmed the review was performed

Material weakness — an executive bypassed all three procurement controls (requisition, PO, GR) and the only compensating control also failed, representing a complete breakdown in the management override control environment
